correctness.rationale: The occupancy counts a_i for matched endpoints in each rung imply \(a_i+a_{i+1}\le2\), yielding the sharp floor(n/2) upper bound. Equality on even cycles forces either two rung patterns or four alternating horizontal patterns (the latter only at multiples of four); their mutual edge symmetric differences are never two. For odd n=2k+1, exactly two units of column-pair deficit force either one adjacent 00 defect (n rung configurations) or two 01 defects bounding a 2ell-column rail block and an alternating zero-rung block (2nk configurations). The specified complete edge lists are verified by comparing the encoded rail/rung edge sets under one replacement: only boundary growth/shrinkage or three unique fixed-horizontal-count boundary changes are allowed. The explicit adjacency rules imply the odd degree spectrum, edge count and connectivity. An independently coded branch-and-bound search in \(L(P_n)^2\) reproduces all full configuration and adjacency sets for n=4..19; it is corroboration rather than the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is not the definition of induced matchings, algorithmic complexity, general strong-degree bounds, or the strong chromatic index of prisms. It is the complete maximum-edge packing family and exchange-graph classification of circular ladders, including exact odd \(n^2\) count, odd complete degree spectrum, and the connected-to-frozen transition. Full text of the highly relevant 2013 induced-matching paper, the 2014 arXiv paper and substantive material of a 2025 component-reconfiguration paper were compared on actual objects and implications; none contains a theorem covering this explicit family. Both available current-week claim ledgers were compared for overlap, including earlier prism strong-edge-coloring and prism total-domination claims. A hidden equivalent result remains possible, but no decisive coverage was found.

value.rationale: A maximum induced matching is an optimal set of mutually noninterfering edges; optimization alone says nothing about whether one selected edge can be replaced while retaining optimality. The theorem answers that mobility question for every circular ladder, giving a complete parity transition: the even optimum configurations are entirely immobile but \(n^2\) odd optima admit a connected local exchange network with a nonregular, exact degree spectrum. The column-deficit decomposition explains this transition structurally rather than restating an existing numerical bound, and the exact neighbor presentation permits explicit transformations and further solution-space study.
